items.title: God of War Laufey SDCC Panel Live Report | Comic Con 2026
items.description: IGN’s live reporting of San Diego Comic-Con 2026 continues, this time from the front row of the God of War Laufey panel.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
IGN’s live reporting of San Diego Comic-Con 2026 continues, this time from the front row of the God of War Laufey panel. The action kicks off on Friday, July 24, at 5.30pm PT / 8.30pm ET / July 25 1.30am UK time, and we’ll be there delivering you all the news via updates below.

We’re expecting God of War Laufey game director Ariel Lawrence and Santa Monica Studio head of creative Cory Barlog to lead an in-depth conversation with the cast, including Deborah Ann Woll (Laufey), Chris Judge (Kratos), Jack Quaid (Phranque), and Perlina Lau (Rue). Sony has said the panelists will share new details about the heroes of God of War Laufey, including behind-the-scenes insights from development and the performance capture that brings each character to life.

While you wait, check out all IGN’s exclusive coverage of God of War Laufey from its reveal in June. We have Lawrence and Barlog discussing why the developer went with Faye as the main character this time instead of Kratos, and we’ve got an explainer on Faye herself if you need a catch-up on her story.

Meanwhile, on Friday, July 24 and Saturday, July 25, IGN will stream live from San Diego with A-list interviews, exclusive reveals, and live coverage of SDCC’s biggest panels and announcements. Our broadcast runs from 3pm PT / 6pm ET to 7pm PT / 10pm ET each day and streams across IGN platforms. Here's our live show schedule.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Five Biggest Reveals From the Lanterns San Diego Comic Con Panel
items.description: The Lanterns panel at San Diego Comic Con revealed a slew of exciting announcements about HBO’s take on the DC hero. Here’s everything we learned.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The Lanterns panel at San Diego Comic Con revealed a slew of exciting announcements about HBO’s take on the DC hero. Here’s everything we learned.

The cast of HBO's Lanterns sat down for an in-depth chat about what viewers can expect from the show, and if there's one thing they made clear, it's that nearly all of them are huge fans of the DC comic. They're extremely dedicated to doing right by the fans, and if there's anything this panel has shown us, it's that they'll have a lot to love when it finally airs in August.

Warning — Spoilers for Lanterns below!

1. Sinestro is in the show.

However, it doesn’t seem like he’s the big baddie behind the series' main conflict… at least, not yet. From what we saw, he’s been holed up in a space prison for some time — though he’s somehow still able to know about Hal Jordan’s movements, as well as the fact that he’s taking on an apprentice (or, as he forces Hal to admit, a replacement).

2. Manhunters are the central villains of the series.

In one clip, exclusively shown at San Diego Comic Con, we saw Hal interrogate an alien masquerading as a former football player, quizzing him on various trivia about pros and famous games. However, when it came to other topics — Harry Potter and Barack Obama, specifically — the manhunter came up blank, leading to a hilarious back-and-forth between the two characters. What’s more, the manhunter claimed to have a nuke-level explosive embedded in his skeleton, saying he was sent to Earth on a top-secret mission. We’ll leave the end of the scene a secret to avoid too many spoilers, but it proves these beings are no small threat to the planet.

3. Nathan Fillion crashed the San Diego Comic Con Panel.

Yep, that’s right — Guy Gardner himself (sans that horrible haircut) showed up midway through the panel to introduce a short clip from the show featuring his character. Thus far, we’re not sure what his role in the series will be, but it seems he’s bringing his signature irreverent flair from Superman into this newest story. (Fillion even wore a shirt that said, ‘Best Gardner Ever,’ clearly leaning into his role as a loveable knucklehead.)

4. Laura Linney is playing a role in HBO’s Lanterns show.

This was one of the last big reveals from the panel. Co-creator Chris Mundy broke the news, saying she will be playing a Guardian, one of the beings in charge of the Green Lantern Corps. He was loath to share any more information, but promised her performance was nothing short of fantastic.

“Yes, Laura's in the show,” Chris said. “Yes, she plays one of the Guardians, who has a lot to say to John about the role of being the Green Lantern. We were very lucky in a lot of ways… I'm not saying anything else, or else this panel will be mad at me.”

Aaron Pierre also chimed in, saying, “She’s like an auntie. She’s a phenomenal artist and creative, and we were massively blessed to have her grace us with her presence and her talent.”

5. The Red Lanterns might make an appearance in the show.

At the tail end of the panel, one final clip was shown, where Hal and John duke it out over who will wear the ring. In the middle of their knock-down, drag-out brawl, a bright red light starts to shine through Hal’s room as a siren blares in the background. The clip cut off right after this, so it’s unclear if the Red Lanterns were behind the light, or if it was the manhunters. Given the color, we couldn’t help but speculate.

These are just a few of the most interesting tidbits revealed during the Lanterns SDCC panel, including an anecdote from Aaron Pierre explaining that he tore his bicep right before his final call to audition for the role of John Stewart.

HBO's Lanterns streams on August 16, 2026.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
San Diego Comic-Con 2026 has arrived, and we here at IGN will not only be covering all the big news coming out of this weekend, but we are also hosting our own live show that will be filled with exclusive reveals, interviews, and much more from your favorite shows, movies, comics, games, anime, and collectibles.

To ensure you don't miss a thing, we'll be rounding up all the biggest moments right here for you, including Marvel Studios' big return to Hall H ahead of Avengers: Doomsday!

Be sure to keep checking back as we'll be updating this roundup as the weekend goes on, and you can also head over to our SDCC watch guide and most anticipated movies and TV shows article to know what to expect!

Five Biggest Reveals From the Lanterns San Diego Comic Con Panel

Lanterns showrunner Chris Mundy and the cast of Lanterns — Kyle Chandler, Aaron Pierre, Garret Dillahunt, and Poorna Jagannathan — joined us at SDCC, and you can check out the five biggest reveals right here (Spoilers Ahead)!

The crew also tested their mettle in a quiz called Green Lantern of Metal Band, and Pierre tells us that he had a grisly bicep injury that nearly cost him his Lanterns role.

Lanterns: Damon Lindelof Explains the One Rule James Gunn Had For the HBO Series

We had the chance to talk to Lanterns co-creators Damon Lindelof and Tom King about James Gunn's rules for adapting comic book super heroes into movies and television, why Guy Gardner is the main Green Lantern, and what happens when a grizzled Lantern vet like Hal Jordan doesn't want to give up his ring to a younger and more capable Jon Stewart.

Dan Houser on Physical Games: If People Want That I Think Companies Should Provide It

After working on games like Grand Theft Auto 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, Dan Houser and Lazlow are now working together again at Absurd Ventures, and the pair stopped by our live show to share updates on their current projects. We also asked them about the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the death of physical media, and more.

items.title: Paramount and Warner Bros. Deal Officially Paused, Could Be on Hold Until June 2027
items.description: Paramount has agreed to postpone its Warner Bros. merger until after the conclusion of an antitrust trial, which could keep the deal from closing until June 2027.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Paramount has agreed to postpone its Warner Bros. merger until after the conclusion of an antitrust trial, which could keep the deal from closing until June 2027.

Paramount agreed to refrain from closing the deal as the antitrust lawsuit recently launched by a coalition of 12 states progresses (via Variety). The update confirms the company won't make its grasp on Warner Bros. official until five days after the case's conclusion or June 2027.

"Today’s agreement is a significant win because the result is exactly what we have sought from the outset: a direct path to a trial based on the evidence," a Paramount spokesperson said in a statement. "This is the fastest and clearest way to prove that this transaction is good for competition, good for consumers, and good for creators, a conclusion dozens of competition authorities around the world have already reached.

"'Plaintiffs' market definitions bear no relationship to the realities of today's marketplace and cannot withstand scrutiny. We look forward to proving our case at trial."

Paramount launched a hostile bid for Warner Bros. just days after Netflix announced it had acquired the HBO company in December of last year. The events that followed eventually saw Netflix exit the acquisition altogether, leaving only Paramount to claim victory.

It's been far from an easy road, however, with many entities emerging to challenge the deal. The 12-state coalition, led by California, launched its suit July 13 in hopes of "fighting for a free and fair market and a thriving film and television industry that serves creatives and audiences alike." Earlier this week, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin ordered a two-week pause for the merger that would see the deal barred from being completed until August. Now, with no trial date set yet, it could be on hold for nearly a year.

"Our argument against this illegal merger is straightforward: When too few corporations have too much power in markets central to American life, it makes things more expensive, and it makes things worse," California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a statement. "Today's agreement is great news for audiences, movie theaters, and the many people who write, build, and create the art, news, and entertainment so many of us enjoy. We are eager to continue to make our case in court and celebrate another tremendous win in our effort to ensure this unlawful merger never sees the light of day."

What started as the latest in a series of smaller roadblocks for Paramount has morphed into what could be a nearly year-long delay for the $110 billion Hollywood deal. As noted by Variety, a delay of this length is quite the blow to Paramount, which had been hoping to close its Warner Bros. merger much earlier. Starting September 30, 2026, the company will begin accumulating a fee of $7 million per day, which will be paid to Warner Bros. investors.

For now, it's unclear when the Paramount-Warner Bros. deal will close. With at least a few months to go as the antitrust lawsuit gets off the ground, Paramount's fight to take over the company is just beginning.

Photo by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images.

items.title: Aaron Pierre Reveals Grisly Bicep Injury That Nearly Cost Him Lanterns Role
items.description: Aaron Pierre explained that he nearly didn’t get his role as John Stewart in HBO’s Lanterns series due to a gnarly bicep injury he sustained mere months before filming.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Aaron Pierre explained that he nearly didn’t get his role as John Stewart in HBO’s Lanterns series due to a gnarly bicep injury he sustained mere months before filming.

Pierre shared the shocking story at the official Lanterns panel at San Diego Comic Con, saying he went to his final callback while his arm was still in a brace while he was recovering from surgery.

“Just before we started filming, my tendon separated from the bone,” he said, drawing sympathetic gasps from the audience. “My bicep went all the way up to my shoulder. This was right at the point where I was gonna finally meet Chris and Damon and Tom. I remember my team gave me a call and said, ‘Look, you have this opportunity. You are in the final two or three.’

“I just had surgery and I'm walking around like this,” he continued, mimicking his arm in a sling. “I can't fully extend my arm. They said, ‘You still wanna do it?’ I said, ‘Don't ask silly questions.’ I went into the callback in my brace."

Throughout the panel, Pierre made his love for the Lanterns extremely clear, even wearing a custom letterman jacket emblazoned with ‘In brightest day, in blackest night’ on the back (as well as some special Green Lantern-themed kicks). For him, playing John Stewart was so important that he would do anything — even show up to his final callback in a brace to prove his dedication to the part.

“I just wanted the role so much,” he said. “I love John so much. I think in that moment — this isn't hyperbole — I was like, ‘What would John do?’ I walked in there and gave it my best. I got the role, and I had a matter of months to rehab. I had a fantastic team.”

Pierre isn't alone is suffering a grisly bicep tear; Ryan Hurst, formerly cast as Kratos in Prime Video's God of War series, was forced to leave the project after tearing his bicep filming a stunt for the show. The role will now be recast, with filming projected to resume in 2027.

HBO’s Lanterns streams on August 16, 2026.

items.title: Brad Bird Debuts New Footage From Ray Gunn and Talks About the Movie's Sci-Fi Noir Approach | Comic Con 2026
items.description: At San Diego Comic-Con, director Brad Bird (The Incredibles, Ratatouille) revealed more about his newest animated film, Ray Gunn, along with debuting the opening seven minutes of the upcoming Netflix release.
items.author: Eric Goldman
items.content:
At San Diego Comic-Con, director Brad Bird (The Incredibles, Ratatouille) revealed more about his newest animated film, Ray Gunn, and debuting the opening seven minutes of the upcoming Netflix release.

Bird was the subject of a spotlight My Cinematic Journey SDCC panel in Hall H, hosted by Collider EIC Steven Weintraub. Bird recounted how his elevator pitch for the film was "Buck Rogers meets The Maltese Falcon," describing it as a film about "desperate characters in an alternate future."

The opening scenes give us a look at the film's setting, a futuristic city filled with giant, brilliantly lit towers and flying cars, but with an art deco/1930s vibe to it. It's like if Coruscant was mashed together with Batman: The Animated Series' Gotham City. We see flying cars with art deco design elements, and businessmen in suit and ties taking off into the air on jet packs, while holding old school briefcases by the handle. Jetpacks are omnipresent, including on construction workers, who use them to float about the building they're working on.

"It's Buck Rogers meets The Maltese Falcon."

Brad Bird previews his new movie #RayGunn at #SDCC. pic.twitter.com/i5nAiqGwBe

— Rotten Tomatoes 🍅 (@RottenTomatoes) July 24, 2026

The brunt of the footage focused on the lanky, one-eyed green alien known as Eyera (voiced by Tom Waits) paying someone off to get a janitor's uniform to sneak into an office where it's revealed his trash can actually contains the title character, Ray Gunn himself (Sam Rockwell). There are shadows aplenty in the noir-infused visuals of the square-jawed, sardonic hero Ray and his pal Eyera searching for secret files, only for a competing duo of aliens showing up to find them as well... and for all four to be interrupted by the large, hulking female alien whose office they're breaking into.

It turns out this lady and Ray know each other, as her four extra arms are revealed during a furious fight that culminates in Ray saving himself by using a freeze ray device in her office to form solid ice around her head. But when Eyera tries to get them to run out of there before the cops arrive, Ray proves he's got a good heart by not letting her suffocate, insisting they stay to smash open the ice first. It takes a bunch of very funny Looney Tunes-style bashes of her head back and forth to crack it open properly.

As he had when he spoke to IGN recently, Bird reiterated the very long journey to get Ray Gunn made, noting it had taken 30 years. "I would have happily made it a long time ago, but you need someone to pay for it," Bird quipped. "I always liked it and always thought it would be a good movie."

Bird stressed the importance of fully building out the film's setting, Metropia, noting the movie takes place nearly entirely in this city, which he described as "sci-fi but very urban." Bird and his animators worked to pack the frames with details. "You can let your eye drift and there will be something for it," he said.

Ray Gunn is scored by Michael Giacchino, who has scored all of Bird's movies since The Incredibles. Giachinno made a surprise appearance at the panel, noting he mixed many elements into the music, saying it included "'50s sci-fi, '30s and '40s noir, some slight jazz.”

He said that his big concern was that the score didn't sound like The Incredibles, but stressed that he loves working with Bird because the director likes to switch things up "and takes a hard left turn with his stuff."

items.title: Chuck Russell, Director Behind A Nightmare on Elm Street 3 and The Mask, Dead at 74
items.description: Chuck Russell, the director behind movies like The Mask and A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors, has died at 74.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Chuck Russell, the director behind movies like The Mask and A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors, has died at 74.

The filmmaker behind some of the most memorable movies of the '80s, '90s, and 2000s unexpectedly passed away at his San Diego-area home Wednesday, July 22, 2026, his family told TMZ. Details regarding his death were not immediately made clear, though the site said that the local fire department was dispatched to his home Wednesday afternoon "following a report of a medical emergency involving an unconscious male."

Russell, born in May 1958, made his directing debut with 1987's A Nightmare on Elm Street 3: Dream Warriors. It brought an impactful start to his career as a director and was immediately followed by his The Blob remake in 1988.

Russell then went on to team with Jim Carrey to deliver quintessential '90s film The Mask in 1994. In 1996 and 2000, he released Eraser and Bless the Child, respectively, and in 2002, helped bring Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson to the big screen with The Scorpion King.

Russell's career as a director then slowed down in the 2000s, with his next project, Fringe, arriving six years later in 2010, and I Am Wrath then premiering in 2016. The final three films he directed were Junglee (2019), Paradise City (2022), and Witchboard (2024).

Russell's The Mask earned an Oscar nomination at the 67th Academy Awards in 1995. Fans of his work have already taken to social media to share their condolences with his family and fond memories of his work.

items.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved Secret Ending Cutscene Suggests a Halo 2 Remake Is on the Way
items.description: Halo Studios seems to have teased a Halo 2 remake in a secret ending cutscene for Halo: Campaign Evolved.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Halo Studios seems to have teased a Halo 2 remake in a secret ending cutscene for Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Microsoft's Halo 1 remake is finally out in the wild for those who gained early access by purchasing its Premium or Collector's Editions. Just one day removed from its early launch, that means many have already blown through the game multiple times, and some have even discovered a tease for a Halo 2 remake.

Those who manage to beat Halo: Campaign Evolved on Legendary difficulty will be greeted with a new secret cutscene featuring none other than Sergeant Johnson (via ComicBook). Beginning by showing him watching a clip from the original secret ending, Johnson ditches the Elite to kick up his feat on the beach. Just after catching an explosion on the ring, he makes his exit, but not before dropping that tease: "See you in the sequel."

As if that wasn't already enough, another post-credits tease offers even more evidence to suggest a Halo 2 remake is in the cards. In the scene, players can see 343 Guilty Spark flying toward a planet, likely to meet up with Arbiter and launch into the events of the original sequel game. YouTube channel GamersPrey uploaded the full ending sequence here.

It wouldn't be a surprise to see Halo Studios and Xbox continue with a follow-up – or maybe even two – now that a re-imagining for the original is here. However, the pair have yet to announce a proper Halo 2 remake, so the future of the series in general mostly remains a mystery, for now.

Last week, YouTuber Rebs Gaming and Windows Central reported that the developer had most recently canceled a Halo multiplayer game. The project was said to be being worked on by Certain Affinity under the codename "Ekur." That leaves Halo: Campaign Evolved as the only game to carry single-player fans of the franchise until more is shared in the future.

Halo 2 launched for the original Xbox in 2004 and received the remaster treatment with the Master Chief Collection in 2014. Halo: Campaign Evolved, meanwhile, will deliver its remake of the first game when it launches July 28, 2026. Until then, and until Halo Studios is willing to share more about its potential future remake plans, you can check out IGN's 7/10 review of the new game.

"Halo: Campaign Evolved speaks to the series' timelessness and adds a decent set of new missions," we said, "but it's mostly a lean retread that's more of a test run for its future with Unreal Engine."

items.title: Incredibles Director Brad Bird's Long-Planned 1906 San Francisco Earthquake Project Could Become a Miniseries | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Brad Bird reveals at San Diego Comic-Con why his long-gestating 1906 San Francisco earthquake movie is now being planned as an eight-episode miniseries.
items.author: Eric Goldman
items.content:
At San Diego Comic-Con Thursday, The Incredibles and Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol director Brad Bird revealed he's looking to turn his long-in-development project about the 1906 San Francisco earthquake into a miniseries.

This project goes way back for Bird, with the first reports that he was considering making it as a feature film dating back to 2007. It was meant to be his live-action debut, but never came to be, with Bird instead making Ghost Protocol.

Bird dismissed what he referred to as "BS stories online" at the time that the movie version was halted because of budget concerns. Instead, he said, it simply was a situation of not being able to figure out how to fit everything he wanted to into one film.

As Bird explained, when he began to research the 1906 quake, "the deeper I dug, the more stuff [I'd find]." At a certain point, he felt like he was cutting too much, which is why a miniseries would be a natural fit. Though he cautioned it would indeed need a large budget because "it has to be big like a movie.”

Bird's comments about the project were made during the Brad Bird: My Cinematic Journey panel at SDCC, hosted by Collider EIC Steven Weintraub. When Weintraub asked how Bird envisions the miniseries, he remarked, "It’s probably like eight episodes. But it has the greatest build ever. It’s not just the earthquake, it’s the fire after earthquake."

He went on to note that the fire that followed the earthquake was fed by giant winds that "got to be like gale force."

Understandably, much of the panel was focused on Bird's next project, the animated movie Ray Gunn releasing on Netflix this fall. Incredibles 3 was also mentioned, with longtime Bird collaborator, composer Michael Giachinno (who also scored Spider-Man: Brand New Day), making a surprise appearance. Bird reiterated that he is not directing Incredibles 3 — Pete Sohn (Elemental) will direct — but he is co-writing (alongside Dana Murray) and producing the project.

As for Giachinno's involvement, when the composer coyly asked who's doing the score, Bird joked, "the ghost of Jerry Goldsmith” before deadpanning: “We’ll talk about it." That's probably a confirmation Giachinno will indeed return for the next installment of the Incredibles franchise.

Bird also mentioned a bit about another project he has in development — one that could potentially happen before the 1906 miniseries. Bird didn't want to reveal many details, but said it was a film he'd direct. “It’s live-action, but there’s animation in it.”

items.title: In The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3, the Balrog Speaks — and It's Simon Pegg | Comic Con 2026
items.description: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 features a creature famous for failing to pass Gandalf in The Fellowship of the Ring — and, for the first time ever, it speaks.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 features a creature famous for failing to pass Gandalf in The Fellowship of the Ring — and, for the first time ever, it speaks.

At San Diego Comic-Con 2026 today, Prime Video debuted a trailer for Season 3 and revealed three new characters: Eddie Marsan (Happy-Go-Lucky) plays King Durin IV’s older brother, Thrain; Andrew Richardson (Guys & Dolls) plays Elendil’s younger son and Isildur’s brother, Anarion; and Adam Young (Don’t Breathe 2) plays Marnûkh, who is described as “a mysterious Orc who may not be what he seems.” They join the previously announced Jamie Campbell Bower as Celeborn, and Zubin Varla as Khamûl the Easterling.

But the headline addition here is Simon Pegg of Shaun of the Dead and Hot Fuzz fame as the voice of The Balrog — yes, The Balrog, Tolkien’s terrifying creature born of fire, darkness, and shadow who battles Gandalf on the bridge of Khazad-dûm. At SDCC, Prime Video debuted an in-room only featurette titled Bringing Season 3’s Creatures to Life, which showed highlights of several creatures that will be seen this season, including Fell-beasts, the war elephants known as Mûmakil, Orcs, and the return of the Balrog, who for the first time ever will speak.

The Balrog does not speak at any point in any of Tolkien’s texts, nor is there an indication in any of his texts that Balrogs generally are able to speak. So The Rings of Power really is doing something quite different here.

You might remember that in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 2, the Balrog was awakened prematurely from its slumber beneath the Misty Mountains by the greedy Dwarves' mining for mithril. King Durin III sacrifices himself in Khazad-dûm to stop the ancient monster after removing his corrupting ring.

In Season 3, Sauron learns the power to forge the One Ring from the Balrog itself. During the SDCC panel featurette, the showrunners described the Balrog as an "intelligent dangerous adversary," adding: "We want to show a different side of him. We are crazy stupid or wild enough to think in this season he should have a scene with Sauron." Is this the same Balrog we saw in Season 2, or a different one? It's unclear at this stage.

The new teaser shows off the “darker tone” Season 3 is going for, as it depicts Sauron’s quest to forge the One Ring. As we know, Jamie Campbell Bower (Stranger Things) plays Galadriel’s long-lost husband, Celeborn, and Zubin Varla (Andor) plays Khamûl the Easterling, of Rhûn, who goes on to become the second-in-command of the Nazgûl and the only Ringwraith besides the Witch-king named explicitly in J.R.R. Tolkien's core writings.

Season 3 features the Nazgnagôl, the earlier Second Age incarnation of the Nazgûl we know from the Third Age. This means we’ll get to see the origins of the Ringwraiths, who were men working for Sauron and lusting for power. It’s worth remembering that The Rings of Power is set thousands of years before the events of J.R.R. Tolkien’s The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings books, so much of what we see in the show is forgotten by the time Gandalf knocks on Bilbo Baggins’ door.

The first four episodes of Season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power will premiere on November 11, 2026. Episodes five and six will be available to stream on November 18, and the final two episodes of the season will be released on November 25.

Now is the mighty hour. Watch the Official Teaser Trailer to The Lord of The Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3, streaming November 11 on Prime Video. pic.twitter.com/3cktqVK8cH

— The Lord of the Rings (@TheRingsofPower) July 24, 2026

Here’s the official blurb:

In Season 3, Middle-earth is at war. Five years have passed since the fall of Eregion. Sauron’s armies have marched across the whole of the world, conquering all in their path. Only a few isolated pockets stand between the Dark Lord and total victory — Khazad-dûm, where the Dwarves are now sealed deep within their mountain halls, and the elven realms of Lindon and Rivendell, which are protected by their Three Rings. But deep in the land of Mordor, in his newly completed tower of Barad-dûr, the Dark Lord toils day and night, obsessed with harnessing a power that will bring the last of his enemies to their knees: One Ring to rule them all... Now, all the free peoples of Middle-earth — Dwarves, Elves, Men, and Wizards alike — must find a way to come together, in a race against time to prevent Sauron from achieving his goal of utter domination of all life…

Amazon says The Rings of Power is one of the highest performing and most-viewed titles ever on Prime Video. Season 1 is the biggest TV series premiere in the history of Prime Video, and Season 2 is among the Top 5 most-watched returning seasons ever. The series has attracted over 185 million viewers worldwide. The Rings of Power is still on-track to run for five seasons, with the $1 billion show reportedly still under the protection of Amazon boss Jeff Bezos' "magical halo" despite its huge costs.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Marvel Is Finally Publishing New Indiana Jones Comics | Comic Con 2026
items.description: At long last, Marvel Comics is kicking off a new line of Indiana Jones comics, starting with Indiana Jones and the Sword of Pandemonium in December.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
It's been well over a decade since Disney acquired Lucasfilm Ltd. And while they wasted no time in taking advantage of the Star Wars franchise on the publishing side, they've been strangely reticent to focus on Indiana Jones. Even when Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny hit theaters in 2023, there was no new Indiana Jones comic to be had. But there's finally some good news on that front, as Marvel has revealed a new Indiana Jones comic launching in December 2026.

The news broke during the Lucasfilm Publishing panel at SDCC 2026. The new series in question is called Indiana Jones and the Sword of Pandemonium. This five-issue limited series is a direct follow-up to the original Raiders of the Lost Ark movie.

Indiana Jones and the Sword of Pandemonium is written by Jason Aaron, who previously helmed Marvel's 2015 Star Wars series. The book is illustrated by Aaron Kuder (Daredevil), and the first issue features cover art by Kuder, Bryan Hitch, and Alex Ross.

Here's the official description for Indiana Jones and the Sword of Pandemonium #1:

In the wake of Indiana Jones and the Raiders of the Lost Ark, Indy’s most notorious villains, including the impossible return of an archenemy, seek a terrifying new source of power to recoup their loss—one that’s fallen into the hands of his former companion, Marion Ravenwood. Now, Indiana Jones has to race to the far corners of the globe in search of a biblical weapon, embarking on an epic quest that will put both his archeology skills and skepticism of the supernatural to the ultimate test!

This new series looks to be the first step in Marvel's larger plans for the Indy franchise, with the solicitation teasing that the book is "Kicking off a new era of Marvel Comics Indiana Jones Storytelling."

What new Indy adventures do you want to see from Marvel? Let us know in the comments.

items.title: The Future's Bright in Blade Runner 2099's Debut Trailer | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Prime Video has revealed Blade Runner 2099 with a debut trailer at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, and confirmed all eight episodes will drop on November 25, 2026.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Prime Video has revealed Blade Runner 2099 with a debut trailer at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, and confirmed all eight episodes will drop on November 25, 2026.

As the title of the show suggests, Blade Runner 2099 is set 50 years after the events of the Ryan Gosling movie, Blade Runner 2049. We return to Los Angeles with the replicants having won out over the humans in an uprising, leaving the replicants in charge and the humans second class citizens.

Cora, played by Euphoria star Hunter Schafer, is a human fugitive who pretends to be a Blade Runner, having run from them all her life. Cora is forced to join forces with Michelle Yeoh’s Olwen, a Replicant Blade Runner days from dying, as the pair hunt a runaway replicant who is hiding a truth that could collapse the city.

Welcome to a future we no longer control. Blade Runner 2099, a new series, premieres November 25 on Prime Video. pic.twitter.com/80nQGY8sFQ

— Prime Video (@PrimeVideo) July 24, 2026

The trailer is dripping with the cyberpunk aesthetic established by Ridley Scott’s influential dystopian future-noir thriller, complete with video ads on skyscrapers and flying cars. Indeed, Scott is an executive producer on the show, working with showrunner Silka Luisa to nail the feel of the series.

To that end, Blade Runner 2099 has a much sunnier look than the dark and rainy 1982 original, or Denis Villeneuve’s cold and snowy 2049, although the trailer does briefly show the city at night and in the rain, the neon-drenched skyline scarred by spinners in flight.

Setting the scene, Schafer's Cora says in the trailer: "We already fought a war. We lost. Replicants, they keep taking it all away. But how much longer until we have nothing? Until we are nothing."

Dimitri Abold (The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes) and Lewis Gribben (Somewhere Boy) are series regulars alongside the aforementioned Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer. Katelyn Rose Downey (The Nun II), Daniel Rigby (Renegade Nell), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow”), Amy Lennox (Only Child), Sheila Atim (The Woman King), Matthew Needham (House of the Dragon), Tom Burke (Furiosa) and Maurizio Lombardi (Ripley) are recurring guest stars.

items.title: Even the Resident Evil Movie Isn't Safe from the PlayStation Physical Disc Controversy
items.description: If you thought the new Resident Evil movie trailer would be safe from the PlayStation physical disc controversy, think again.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
If you thought the new Resident Evil movie trailer would be safe from the PlayStation physical disc controversy, think again.

The latest teaser video for director Zach Cregger's live-action Resident Evil adaptation was immediately flooded with negative comments published on the PlayStation YouTube channel yesterday. It's the latest example in the weeks of outrage that have followed Sony's decision to kill support for physical discs in 2028.

While most gamers have directed the backlash to gaming-related announcements, Resident Evil's status as a film doesn't seem to have deterred angry fans hoping to make their voices heard. Of the 1,800 comments left below the PlayStation upload for the trailer, most of the "Top" messages reference the controversy in one way or another. Some are more clever than others.

"I cannot wait to get the physical version of this," one fan, echoing the comments left on other PlayStation videos, said.

"He’s transporting the last physical game copy in existence," another joked.

"Leon…. Where are the Physical Discs?" someone else said.

PlayStation social media accounts have served as a hub for fans to voice their…feelings about Sony's physical strategy since the company made its initial announcement July 1, 2026. The move will see it cease production for new physical video games starting January 2028, meaning titles launched after the cutoff date will be completely restricted to a digital release. Players, especially those who have spent the last 50ish years collecting and trading physical versions of games, aren't happy, to say the least.

After a short social media hiatus, PlayStation returned to X/Twitter and was immediately swarmed by angry comments. Every post since then has faced a similar level of backlash, with the outrage spreading to other sites, too. The Marvel's Wolverine game is the latest example of a game trailer to be flooded by those calling for change.

It's not too surprising to see the PlayStation upload for the Resident Evil trailer filled with comments. While the vast majority of the backlash seems to have stuck to PlayStation channels, even other comment sections aren't free from references to physical game discs.

"I cant wait for the physical edition!" one viewer replied on the Sony Pictures version of the video.

The Resident Evil movie is only the latest to fall victim to the controversy, but it's not the first time it's found itself in the line of fire. Longtime fans were disappointed to see Cregger had taken some creative liberties when it comes to the Raccoon City Incident when they laid eyes on its first teaser in April, for example.

This looks so good but also pic.twitter.com/2KlEuvbGBS

— 𝙈𝙖𝙧𝙭 𝙒𝙖𝙨 𝙍𝙞𝙜𝙝𝙩 ☭ (@karlmarxisright) July 23, 2026

Im hyped but 👇 pic.twitter.com/bvhRGY9DjK

— SIDTYPE (@ghost42_00) July 23, 2026

The Weapons director will bring his Resident Evil to theaters September 18, 2026. For more, you can read about some of the Easter Eggs tucked into the new trailer. You can also read about how Sony may have been prepared for the backlash, and why it's unlikely to U-turn.

items.title: Tomb Raider: Catalyst Delay to 2028 Confirmed by Amazon Games Boss
items.description: Tomb Raider: Catalyst is indeed delayed to 2028, as many had suspected.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Tomb Raider: Catalyst is indeed delayed to 2028, as many had suspected.

Confirmation comes from Amazon’s video game boss, Jeffrey Gattis, who told The Game Business that Catalyst is now due out in 2028, with Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis due out February 12, 2027.

“Atlantis comes February 12 of next year, and then we'll follow on in 2028 with the next one,” Gattis said. No firmer launch window was offered.

Both games were announced at the same time, in December last year. Catalyst is the next-gen, Unreal Engine 5-built Tomb Raider that developer Crystal Dynamics announced years ago now. In December, it was set for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S in 2027, published by Amazon Game Studios. Here's the official blurb:

Tomb Raider: Catalyst marks a bold direction for the series as Lara Croft embarks on a new adventure across Northern India. Tomb Raider: Catalyst is set in the wake of a mythical cataclysm that has unleashed ancient secrets and awakened the mysterious forces that guard them. When the most notorious treasure hunters from around the world descend on the region, Lara races to uncover the truth buried beneath the fractured landscape and stop those who would use its power for their own gain. As the ancient world collides with the present, Lara must decide who to trust among rivals and allies to prevent a catastrophe and protect a secret that could reshape the future.

In June, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis was delayed from this year to February 12, 2027 release date. Alix Wilton Regan plays Lara Croft in both games, replacing Camilla Luddington, who portrayed Lara Croft in the Survivor Trilogy.

In March, Crystal Dynamics suffered its fourth redundancy round in 12 months, although the Embracer-owned studio insisted it remained “fully committed to the future development" of the Lara Croft franchise. The upcoming Tomb Raider games are published by Amazon, which is also working on a Tomb Raider TV show for Prime Video starring Game of Thrones’ Sophie Turner.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: PlayStation Network Back Online After Outage Causes PSN Users to Lose Access to Their Games for Hours
items.description: Sony's PlayStation Network services have been offline for hours today, leaving fans unable to play some digital games. Unsurprisingly, impacted users have been left pointing to the benefits of physical copies — just weeks after Sony's bombshell announcement it will kill PS5 discs.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
UPDATE 12:10 p.m. PT: All PlayStation Network services are now back online after an outage caused PSN to go down for hours this morning.

The PlayStation Service Status Page reports that "all services are up and running." Issues related to the PlayStation Store have been resolved, and players have returned to playing their games.

IGN will add to this page with any updates from Sony.

UPDATE 12:00 p.m. PT: It appears the PlayStation Network is back online after being down for hours this morning.

Sony has updated its PlayStation Status page to reflect that its account management, gaming and social, PlayStation Video, and PlayStation Direct services are back up and running. The page also notes that players may still "have difficulty getting products on the PlayStation Store," but Sony said it is "working to resolve the issue as soon as possible."

Sony has not clarified what caused the lengthy PSN outage. Players across social media have started to report that they can access the network again. We'll continue to update this page with any additional information.

ORIGINAL STORY: Sony's PlayStation Network services have been offline for hours today, leaving fans unable to play some digital games. Unsurprisingly, impacted users have been left pointing to the benefits of physical copies — just weeks after Sony's bombshell announcement it will kill PS5 discs.

PlayStation services began to disappear for some users around 8.30am Eastern this morning, around the same time as an alert from Amazon Web Services that "multiple AWS servers in the US-WEST-2 region" were facing "connectivity issues." Despite the problem being marked as resolved around an hour later, players report continued experiencing continued issues in the hours since — and in countries outside the U.S., too.

The issue has hit PlayStation services just as the open beta for the Sony-published (and console exclusive) Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls was getting underway, with its developer subsequently acknowledging issues on PS5.

At the time of writing, Sony's own service status page continues to show errors across every PlayStation network service, from playing and purchasing digital content, streaming games, account management services and more.

"You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features," Sony wrote on its official status page, with impacted platforms listed as including PS Vita, PS3, PS4 and PS5. "We're working to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience."

While outages happen, the timing for this latest interruption of service could not be much worse. As well as impacting Marvel Tōkon, a key title for Sony, the disruption comes as the firestorm of controversy over Sony's decision to kill discs is still very much aflame. This month has seen Sony continually slammed by PlayStation fans for its hugely unpopular decision to discontinue launching new PS5 games via physical discs from January 2028 onwards — a choice that has sparked an enormous petition, endless social media posts, and a stream of angry commentary on every trailer or livestream that the console maker now hosts.

Only last night, Sony uploaded new footage of its promising-looking exclusive Marvel's Wolverine — though the YouTube comments are full of further outrage at the disc situation. Analysts and even former Sony staff say that the situation is highly unlikely to change, but regardless — fans are not letting this one go anytime soon, and a moment that highlights one of the pitfalls of gaming's all-digital future has today only underlined its downsides further.

"We had ourselves a lovely PSN outage, we see," wrote gaming accessibility service Does it Play?, which champions physical game media. "Just one of many things that can go wrong with an all-digital future in the way Sony's shapes up to be. Be careful what you wish for."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Total War: Warhammer 40,000 Has the Biggest Unit Ever in a Total War Game — and of Course It Belongs to the Orks
items.description: Total War: Warhammer 40,000 developer Creative Assembly has shown off a full battle in the upcoming strategy game, and in doing so confirmed it features the biggest unit ever in a Total War game.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Total War: Warhammer 40,000 developer Creative Assembly has shown off a full battle in the upcoming strategy game, and in doing so confirmed it features the biggest unit ever in a Total War game.

The livestream included lots of interesting discussion about unit cards, shooting, suppression, flanking, and equipment, but what caught my eye was bigger than all that put together.

“We really wanted to put the biggest thing that we could get away with in a Total War game,” David Petry, battle product owner, said during the stream as the Orks’ towering Stompa came into view.

“We are looking at putting bigger things in later down the line, of course. But this will be the biggest thing we’ve had in a Total War. So, very excited about that.”

What is a Stompa? Well, like most Ork machinations, the Stompa is a crude coming together of bits and bobs that is far greater than the sum of its parts (Ork magic, don't get me started). It is a walking, shooting battle fortress that, as you’d expect from its name, stomps all over the battlefield, crushing all that gets in its way. It has a crew of several Orks, dozens of Grot riggers, runners, and assistants, and usually two or three enormous guns and a gigantic claw for melee. If you’re an enemy tank, you need to be afraid of a Stompa. Well, if you’re anything, you need to be afraid of a Stompa.

In the livestream, the hapless Astra Militarum try to destroy the Stompa with an orbital strike — an extremely powerful attack you won’t be able to use very often. It’s basically an ‘in case of emergency break glass’ move. The Stompa somehow survives the attack, much to the surprise of the developers. But it’s basically dead, and it isn’t long before it blows up.

Petry said that CA is working on adding even bigger units to Total War: Warhammer 40,000 in the future, which is an exciting thought. What could they be? A Titan? A Tyranid Bio Titan? (I’m sure the game will get the Tyranids eventually.) Something else?

Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is still without a release date, but we're getting plenty of news from CA on a regular basis now. This week, we reported on all the named characters announced for Total War: Warhammer 40,000 so far, after Games Workshop confirmed Ork Warboss Nazdreg Ug Urdgrub is in the game. How the named characters work in-game, however, we don't know.

“We really wanted to put the biggest thing that we could get away with in a Total War game,” David Petry, battle product owner, said during the stream as the Orks’ towering Stompa came into view.

“We are looking at putting bigger things in later down the line, of course. But this will be the biggest thing we’ve had in a Total War. So, very excited about that.”

What is a Stompa? Well, like most Ork machinations, the Stompa is a crude coming together of bits and bobs that is far greater than the sum of its parts (Ork magic, don't get me started). It is a walking, shooting battle fortress that, as you’d expect from its name, stomps all over the battlefield, crushing all that gets in its way. It has a crew of several Orks, dozens of Grot riggers, runners, and assistants, and usually two or three enormous guns and a gigantic claw for melee. If you’re an enemy tank, you need to be afraid of a Stompa. Well, if you’re anything, you need to be afraid of a Stompa.

In the livestream, the hapless Astra Militarum try to destroy the Stompa with an orbital strike — an extremely powerful attack you won’t be able to use very often. It’s basically an ‘in case of emergency break glass’ move. The Stompa somehow survives the attack, much to the surprise of the developers. But it’s basically dead, and it isn’t long before it blows up.

Petry said that CA is working on adding even bigger units to Total War: Warhammer 40,000 in the future, which is an exciting thought. What could they be? A Titan? A Tyranid Bio Titan? (I’m sure the game will get the Tyranids eventually.) Something else?

Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is still without a release date, but we're getting plenty of news from CA on a regular basis now. This week, we reported on all the named characters announced for Total War: Warhammer 40,000 so far, after Games Workshop confirmed Ork Warboss Nazdreg Ug Urdgrub is in the game. How the named characters work in-game, however, we don't know.

items.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Will Introduce the Ringwraiths, And Has Invented an Early Version Named the Nazgnagôl
items.description: The Rings of Power will continue introducing more elements from The Lord of the Rings by showing early versions of the Ringwraiths, re-invented as the Nazgnagôl.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The Rings of Power will continue introducing more elements from The Lord of the Rings by showing early versions of the Ringwraiths, re-invented as the Nazgnagôl.

Amazon's ambitious Lord of the Rings prequel will return for its third season later this year, now with Sauron ruling over swathes of Middle-earth. The nine human rulers previously given rings have now been corrupted, and while they are not yet the Ringwraiths seen in the Third Age, they will be shown as well on their way.

Tolkien named this group the Nazgul, though the Rings of Power's showrunners are adopting a slightly different name for their proto versions: the Nazgnagôl, which means "Ring-servant."

"We love looking back at what inspired Tolkien," showrunner J.D. Payne told Empire. "He led with language. Language became a scaffold on which the myth would hang. The word Nazgul means Ringwraith in the Black Speech of Mordor. But before they were Ringwraiths, we know that these were just men. So we were able to derive in the Black Speech that nagôl could mean servant. Nazgnagôl, therefore, literally means Ring-servant."

Only two of the Nine were ever named by Tolkien: the fearsome Witch-king of Angmar, and his second-in-command: Khamûl, the Black Easterling, who will be played in the upcoming season by British stage actor Zubin Varla.

"Every character stays the hero of their own story," Payne concludes. "From Khamûl's point of view, he is a warlord who deserves to be a king, whose power has been usurped by a dark wizard. Sauron offers him a way back to the top."

This appears to suggest an intertwining of the meandering subplot featuring the halflings and Gandalf in the east, where Khamûl is from, with the series' more central plotlines. Curiously, there has been no mention yet at all of the halflings returning for the series' third season. Meanwhile, the identity of the Dark Wizard remains a mystery — though it is believed he is likely one of the two Blue Wizards left out of Tolkien's main work.

Earlier this week, we learned that Galadriel's husband Celeborn will also finally be introduced in the show's next season. The role is set to be portrayed by Stranger Things' Jamie Campbell Bower, who described the character as acting like a "lover-boy."

Rings of Power is still on-track to run for five seasons, with the $1 billion Prime Video show claimed to be still under the protection of Amazon boss Jeff Bezos' "magical halo" despite its huge costs.

items.title: 'It's Good to Be Back': Johnny Depp Meets Fans as Ebenezer Scrooge, as First Trailer Drops for His Big Hollywood Return | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Johnny Depp has returned to the Hollywood limelight with a surprise appearance at Comic-Con in character as Ebenezer Scrooge.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Johnny Depp has returned to the Hollywood limelight with a surprise appearance at San Diego Comic-Con in character as Ebenezer Scrooge.

The Pirates of the Caribbean and Edward Scissorhands star greeted fans in full costume and makeup as the Dickensian antihero, who he'll play in this year's star-studded Christmas movie Ebenezer — a project widely seen as Depp's big Hollywood comeback.

Ebenezer will also feature Ian McKellen, Daisy Ridley, Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough and Tramell Tillman in a new twist on the beloved Christmas tale, though all eyes will be on Depp in its starring role — his first major Hollywood part in nearly a decade, following the widely-publicized legal troubles with ex-wife Amber Heard.

This week has seen fans given their best look yet at Depp as Scrooge, via a new trailer (above) and a couple of in-person appearances at Comic-Con. Depp appeared at a pop-up recreation of his house, chatting away with onlookers and eventually dropping the character's signature catchphrase of "humbug" to cheers (you can see this in the video below). The actor then popped up unexpectedly during the event's Directors on Directing panel to reveal Ebenezer's trailer to the audience.

After years focusing on smaller projects and international films, the path now seems to be opening up for Depp to make a career comeback — though a question mark still hangs over whether he will ever resume his most iconic role: Pirates of the Caribbean's Captain Jack Sparrow.

Disney has long had plans to continue its buccaneer movie franchise, and producer Jerry Bruckheimer has talked positively of wanting Depp back. Speaking last year, Bruckheimer confirmed "some" previous Pirates of the Caribbean actors would return for the next movie, while offering "a new take" on the franchise overall.

Whether this actually happens, however, remains to be seen — though a positive response to Ebenezer when it arrives this November 13 may change that.

Image credit: Daniel Knighton/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures

items.title: PlayStation Killing Discs Has Upsides, Ubisoft Boss Yves Guillemot Says, Pointing to Cheaper Consoles Without Disc Drives
items.description: Sony's controversial decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs could have some upsides, Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot has said.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Sony's controversial decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs could have some upsides, Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot has said.

Speaking yesterday during the company's most recent investor Q&A, Guillemot was asked by an analyst for his thoughts on Sony's bombshell announcement that it would discontinue discs for new PS5 games from January 2028 onwards, announced earlier this month.

Perhaps predictably, Guillemot did not strike too downbeat a tone in his answer — in contrast to the huge wave of negative backlash from fans that has been seen online, across social media, livestream comments and an enormous petition. Indeed, Guillemot suggested that some positives would come from the move.

"What we saw on the PC is that it helped to grow the market," Guillemot noted. "There's also some pressure for the future on the cost of machines and being able to be only digital will help to have a more accessible machine, I would say."

Ultimately, Guillemot concluded that Sony's decision would likely not impact the wider industry too much — regardless of the passionate response by actual gamers, which Sony is seemingly doing its best job right now of ignoring.

"There are plus and minus," the Ubisoft CEO concluded, "but we think it will not disturb too much the industry."

Guillemot's comments reflect the fact that the vast majority of game purchases are already digital, following the rise of downloads over the past decade. Indeed, Sony's rationale for ditching discs is that it's simply following consumer trends. "In response to shifting trends in consumer preference, new games will be released on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only," Sid Shuman, Senior Director, Sony Interactive Entertainment Content Communications, said in a post on PlayStation Blog, effectively telling gamers that this outcome was in a response to their own spending habits.

"As consumer preferences and the broader entertainment industry continue to shift away from physical discs to digital, physical game disc production for all new games releasing on PlayStation consoles will be discontinued starting January 2028. Following this date, new games will be available on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only. This transition has no impact on games that already released, or will be releasing, prior to January 2028 in disc format.

"This is a natural direction for Sony Interactive Entertainment to adapt to consumer trends as the general preference for digital media significantly outpaces physical discs. This transition will enable us to align more closely with how most of our community prefers to access and play games today."

Still, the online blowback to Sony's announcement has been huge, with the most vocal proponents of physical releases leading the charge, citing concerns over game ownership and preservation among the key issues. This week, a former God of War developer revealed that Sony knew its decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs would spark outrage, and reportedly issued staff with the "strictest" social media guidelines to stop them from publicly commenting on the controversy.

But Sony seems unlikely to change course, and it has already begun reassigning staff involved with disc production. Cruically, Sony simply earns more money from digital games — at a time when consoles sales are being impacted by rising costs. For a first-party PlayStation game such as The Last of Us, Sony will only keep around 65% of the money from a physical copy, with around 30% going to the retailer and roughly another 5% on manufacturing costs. Meanwhile, for a physical copy of a third-party game such as the Activision-published Call of Duty, Sony will get a licensing fee, likely around 15%. For digital sales, Sony keeps 100% of first-party game revenue, and a far better cut from third-party titles.

Like it or not — and many won't — financially it's hard to argue with Guillemot's assessment, even if it will likely only stir up more frustration among fans. Speaking to IGN, analysts have all said similar. Dr. Serkan Toto, CEO of Japanese game industry consultancy firm Kantan Games, suggested that even if half a million people cancelled their PlayStation Plus subscription in protest, it would be just a drop in the ocean for Sony.

"I sympathize with physical media fans, but Sony will not reverse this decision," Toto told IGN. "They of course knew what the online reaction would look like, and they now wait for this storm to pass.

"Sony has over 120 million active PlayStation users," he continued. "Around 50 million people subscribe to PlayStation Plus. As a thought experiment, let's say 500,000 cancel in protest, that would be just 1% of that business gone — of course not enough for Sony to start rethinking. Digital is just too lucrative."

Image credit: Nathan Laine/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: 'One Day, I'm Sure': Spider-Man: Brand New Day Star Tom Holland Teases Venom Symbiote
items.description: Tom Holland has teased a return of the Venom Symbiote, as the hours count down to the launch of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Tom Holland has teased a return of the Venom Symbiote, as the hours count down to the launch of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

Asked by a young fan if Holland's Spider-Man would ever encounter the Symbiote, Holland said he couldn't answer the question directly — but added that the moment would come "one day, I'm sure."

"We'll get to see the Symbiote," Holland continued, in a moment posted to Instagram by cinempolismx.

Could the Symbiote appear in Brand New Day? It's a question that fans have been debating ever since the movie's first trailer showed Holland's webslinger emerging from a sticky cocoon, with mention that he was undergoing some form of transformation.

Remember, of course, that Spider-Man: No Way Home concluded with a brief shot of the Symbiote — or a part of it — being left behind in the MCU following that film's various multiversal shenanigans. The possibility is certainly there for more from the Symbiote, and many fans see Holland donning a black Symbiote suit as inevitable before he ends his run.

With Brand New Day already stuffed full of foes, the only question seems to be when the Symbiote storyline will be adapted. Could Holland be infected at the end of Brand New Day, with the transformation happening off-screen — potentially explaining his absence in this year's Avengers: Doomsday? That could leave him ready and powered-up to make a triumphant return in 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars.

Alternatively, the widely-expected future films in Holland's second trilogy of Spider-Man movies could center on the Symbiote — perhaps changing Peter Parker's personality just as his identity is restored in the memories of best pal Ned and ex-girlfriend MJ. Let's just hope this incarnation of Peter Parker leaves the dance moves at home, though.

With previews early next week and its official July 31 release date fast approaching, Holland is currently in the middle of a whirlwind Spider-Man: Brand New Day press tour, and proving as chatty as ever. Yesterday, Holland raised eyebrows by flatly denying Jean Grey was in the movie — despite huge speculation that this is who Sadie Sink is playing. The actor has also teased that the movie's title will be explained in its final frame (intriguing!), revealed that "one person" still remembers Peter Parker is Spider-Man (Sadie Sink?) and discussing his potential involvement in the upcoming Avengers movies — which he strongly suggested he will feature in.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social
